statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is 20%, inside the watch band and below the block threshold.
recommendation: Conditions describe a low-volatility trend-up session in which the Nasdaq-100 has printed a marginal new session high and then retraced from it, so mean reversion is observably available. The narrow danger window is the 12:30-14:00Z August employment report on 4 September; outside that window the mapped state stays below the block threshold.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds a 1% gain after a marginal new high and a first retracement, with August payrolls the next binary
body: The Nasdaq-100 trades at 29,451 (+1.06%) inside a 29,161-29,494 session range, having printed a marginal new high at 29,494 and retraced roughly 43 points from it. That retracement is the first of the session and indicates mean reversion is available again, which eases Tail slightly from the prior hour. VIX is 14.61, down 3.9% and sitting at its own session low, while the 2-year yield is 4.34% and the 10-year 4.75%, both lower after Fed Governor Waller pointed to encouraging disinflation and signalled he could support holding the policy rate steady. September hike odds have moved to roughly a coin flip. Today's data was supportive: ISM Services beat at 55.4 against 54.3 consensus, initial jobless claims printed 206K, and Challenger reported 52,881 August job cuts, the lowest August total since 2022. Software leads while semiconductors lag, with Broadcom down about 4% despite an earnings beat; Nvidia gained after confirming a $13 billion acquisition of Hugging Face. Cross-asset alignment is only partial: gold is sharply higher, WTI is near $91.5 with Brent above $95 on renewed US-Iran hostilities around the Strait of Hormuz, and the dollar has fallen more than 2% against the yen to its weakest since late February. Decaying realised volatility, lagging semiconductors and an observed retracement keep Tail below the block threshold, while the dollar dislocation, elevated oil and tomorrow's payrolls binary hold Stress in the elevated band.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 hours the published state was green for 18 of the 19 assessed hours, with Tail between 11% and 15% through the US afternoon, the overnight session and European hours in normal mode as Stress eased into the low 50s. The US morning shifted to mixed as the Waller comments and the ISM Services beat repriced yields, and the most recent published hour moved to yellow with Tail at 21% as the index printed at its session extreme. Five hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The near path keeps Tail at the lower edge of the watch band while the trend-up session persists, with the Hammack speech at 19:00Z and the 20:00Z cash close as checkpoints, and eases below that band once the closing impulse decays. Risk is projected to sit in the low teens through the Asian session, then rebuild through European hours into the August employment report at 12:30Z on 4 September, which is the mapped danger window. Tail is deliberately capped at the top of the watch band across that release, because event magnitude and forecast dispersion raise Stress and lower Confidence rather than establishing a no-retracement price path.
